name: Atlas

hero.title: Write the component. Atlas writes the scenarios and tests every one.
hero.lede: Atlas reads your Pyreon components and their prop types, derives a scenario for every variant, and runs six checks on each: accessibility, interaction, leaks, SSR parity, reactivity coverage and a visual snapshot. You get a workbench, a static docs site and a catalog your coding agent can read, and a check that could not run is reported as not run, never as passed.

why.title: A catalog that cannot drift, because nobody writes it.

items.title: Scenarios come from your types
items.text: A `variant?: 'solid' | 'soft' | 'outline' | 'ghost'` prop becomes a select control and three scenarios. Rocketstyle dimensions become axes too. Add a value to the union and the next scan has a scenario for it.

items.title: Every scenario is mounted, clicked and hydrated
items.text: The scan mounts each scenario, clicks everything interactive, renders it on the server, hydrates it and compares the DOM. `atlas verify-browser` adds axe-core, reactivity coverage and pixel snapshots in real Chromium.

items.title: Three verdicts, never two
items.text: pass, fail or unverified. The summary line names which of the six checks ran (`checks: a11y 7/8 ✗ · interaction 8/8 …`) and the `not run:` line says why the rest did not. A red scan is a red exit code.

items.title: Your coding agent reads the same catalog
items.text: `atlas-agent-guide.md` lists every component's legal prop values and a known-good usage. `atlas check Button '{"variant":"solidd"}'` answers "did you mean `solid`?" and exits 1. MCP serves it as `get_atlas_catalog` and `get_atlas_component`.

difference.title: Seven stories to maintain, or zero.

before.label: Storybook (CSF3)
before.caption: One export per state, rewritten whenever the props change.

after.label: with Atlas
after.caption: The component is the only file. Real scan output underneath.

comingFrom.title: A play function becomes one authored scenario. The variant stories disappear.
comingFrom.note: Atlas runs `play` instead of its automatic click-walk, and a throw fails the interaction check naming the step: `play failed at step "click Save": no button rendered`. It hands you `root` and `step` and no assertion library, so throw (or bring your own `expect`). The same `scenarios` key works in the `atlas` section of `pyreon.config.ts`.

extraSectionsHtml:
real output

What a scan says, word for word.

The examples/atlas-workshop app in the repo: 11 components, no story files, one authored play script. Run under bun, so the leak check runs too.

$ atlas scan .
atlas: discovered 11 component(s), 44 scenario(s) — 42 verified, 2 failing, 0 unverified.
  checks: a11y 12/14 ✗ · interaction 44/44 · ssrParity 44/44 · leak 44/44
  not run: reactivityCoverage, snapshot — browser-only — run `atlas verify-browser` to measure this (a Node scan cannot)
  → atlas-catalog.json
  → atlas-agent-guide.md
atlas: 2 file(s) import a module supplied by a build plugin Atlas does not run (virtual:zero/routes) — typically app entry points.
  Nothing to fix: the import is correct. Atlas cannot load these files, so a component
  defined in one of them would be absent — move it to its own file if you want it catalogued.
atlas: 2 failing scenario(s):
  ✗ button--empty
      a11y [missing-accessible-name]: missing accessible name: "label" is empty
        → Give "label" a non-empty value, or an aria-label if the text is genuinely decorative.
  ✗ badge--empty
      a11y [missing-accessible-name]: missing accessible name: "label" is empty
        → Give "label" a non-empty value, or an aria-label if the text is genuinely decorative.
  Run `atlas verify <Component>` to re-check one component on its own.
$ echo $?
1
already on storybook?

Keep it. Pyreon renders there too.

@pyreon/storybookframework

Set framework: '@pyreon/storybook' and your Pyreon components render in Storybook with Meta, StoryObj, args, decorators and play functions. Atlas never asks you to migrate stories; run both and move when you want to.

demo.title: The workbench, live.
demo.text: This is the Atlas workbench on a small sample library. Pick a component, change its props in Controls, open the A11y tab, and select the Empty scenario: its verdict dot turns red, and the A11y tab names the problem, a button with no accessible name, with axe-core one click away.
demo.spec: Embed the static workbench `atlas build` produces for a small sample library, or mount the real `Workbench` from `@pyreon/atlas/ui` with a `WorkbenchCatalog` whose components carry their `render` function and whose scenarios carry the verdict `atlas scan` wrote (bundle the scan JSON at build time and merge it in). Sidebar shows a verdict dot per scenario (ok, fail, unverified). Selecting Button → Empty shows a red (fail) dot, and the A11y tab's live structural check shows the danger row "Accessible name: interactive element with no name". Controls edit props live; the A11y tab can run axe-core on the preview. Nothing in the demo is a static screenshot of a verdict.

features.title: Workbench, CI gate and agent catalog in one tool.

api.title: Flags, config and the programmatic API.

limits.title: Two and a half checks need a browser
limits.text: Reactivity coverage and snapshots, and the axe-core half of a11y, run in `atlas verify-browser` (needs `playwright-core`). A plain scan marks them not run and says so.

limits.title: The leak check needs a GC hook
limits.text: Run the scan under bun, or node with `--expose-gc`. Without one the leak check skips with that reason rather than passing.

limits.title: Overlays and parts need a hint
limits.text: Components that return null on the server go in `browserOnly`; parts that only render inside a parent go in `parts: { TabPanel: 'Tabs' }`.

limits.title: Pyreon components only
limits.text: Atlas finds Pyreon component shapes and rocketstyle chains. It does not catalog React or Vue components, and `styled('div')` components are not discovered yet.

recipes.title: Gate pull requests on the catalog
recipes.text: The scan exits 1 when any scenario fails a check. `verify-browser` writes axe-core and coverage verdicts into the catalog and exits 1 on a visual diff. Baselines are machine-specific, so this workflow records them on `main` and restores them from the runner cache for every pull request; without a stored baseline the first run only records one.
recipes.code:
# .github/workflows/components.yml
name: components
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
jobs:
  atlas:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
      - run: bun install
      - run: bunx atlas scan .            # exit 1 on any failing check
      - run: bunx playwright-core install chromium
      # baselines are machine-specific: keep them in the runner's cache, recorded on main
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: atlas-snapshots
          key: atlas-snapshots-${{ runner.os }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: atlas-snapshots-${{ runner.os }}-
      # exit 1 on a visual diff; axe-core and coverage verdicts go into atlas-catalog.json
      - run: bunx atlas verify-browser . ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && '--update-snapshots' || '' }}

recipes.title: Stop an agent shipping `variant="solidd"`
recipes.text: A wrong prop value typechecks in plenty of places and renders as nothing. `atlas check` reads the committed catalog, so it answers instantly, and exits 1. Put it in a pre-commit hook or your agent's loop. Output below is from the atlas-workshop example.
recipes.code:
$ atlas check Button '{"label":"Save","variant":"solidd"}'
Button: 1 problem(s):
  · `variant` must be one of `solid`, `soft`, `outline`, `ghost` — got `solidd` — did you mean `solid`?

$ atlas check Button '{"variant":"soft","colour":"red"}'
Button: 2 problem(s):
  · `colour` is not a prop of Button
  · `label` is required and was not supplied

$ atlas check Button '{"label":"Save","variant":"soft","size":"lg"}'
Button: usage is valid.

recipes.title: Publish your design system as a static site
recipes.text: One URL per component, no server. The Docs source block and the Reactivity Lens are computed at build time and shipped as data, so the deployed site still shows real verdicts.
recipes.code:
$ atlas build --out atlas-dist --base /design-system/
# then deploy atlas-dist/ to GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare or S3

faq.q: Do I have to give up Storybook?
faq.a: No. `@pyreon/storybook` renders Pyreon components in Storybook with the usual `Meta`, `StoryObj`, args and play functions. Atlas never imports your stories and never asks you to delete them.

At least one check ran on that scenario and none failed. That is why the scan prints a per-check tally and a `not run:` line: a Node scan runs four of the six checks (three if there is no GC hook), and `atlas verify-browser` runs the rest. A scenario where nothing ran is unverified, never verified.

faq.q: Does it run my component code?
faq.a: Yes, by default: the scan imports each component through Vite to mount it. `atlas scan --no-mount` stays static and never executes component modules; the runtime checks then report as not run.

faq.q: Can it check React or Vue components?
faq.a: No. Atlas reads Pyreon component shapes (function components, `nativeCompat` wrappers, rocketstyle chains). For a mixed codebase, keep Storybook for the rest.

faq.q: How long does a scan take?
faq.a: The atlas-workshop example (11 components, 44 scenarios) scanned in under two seconds on our laptop, one run. The leak check forces garbage collection once per group of about 256 scenarios rather than once per scenario, which is what keeps large libraries fast.

end.title: Point it at your components. Find out which ones were never tested.
